title.en: Drawing a perfect square without tracing

text.en:
"How can I guarantee all four corners of my house blueprint are exact 90° and equal lengths?" asked Kiran.
"Bring out your compass and ruler!" smiled Dad.

A compass is not just for circles—it is the master tool for copying exact distances! Opening the compass sets a fixed radius so every point on the circle sits at the exact same distance from its centre.
To construct a square or rectangle cleanly with a ruler and protractor/set-square, measure lengths accurately and make perpendicular 90° corners.
Even better, compass arcs locate exact intersection points—like finding a roof peak equidistant from two corners, or checking that a rectangle's two diagonals are equal and bisect each other!
Drawing neat geometric shapes means making lengths exact and corners truly square—not just sketching freehand!
Start with a Compass: plant the sharp metal tip at centre O, open to radius r, and sweep smoothly to draw a Circle.

board.text: Circle: all points are radius r from centre

text.en: Remember: even a tiny part of a circle drawn with a compass is called an Arc—and every point on an arc shares that exact distance!

board.text: Arc = compass swing of fixed radius

text.en: Want to copy segment AB onto a line without reading tiny marks? Open your compass to fit A–B, lift carefully and mark that exact length!
Now build a Rectangle ABCD: draw base AB, raise exact 90° perpendicular sides at A and B using a set square or protractor, and mark equal heights AD and BC!
Join A to C and B to D—every rectangle's two diagonals have the exact same length and slice each other right in half!
For a Square, make adjacent sides equal (AB = AD), and its diagonals meet cleanly at 90° right angles too!
How do you build a 'house' roof apex 5 cm from BOTH endpoints P and Q of a 6 cm wall? Draw two 5 cm compass arcs from P and Q!

board.text: Equidistant point = where two arcs cross

text.en: Wherever the two 5 cm arcs intersect sits at exact distance 5 cm from P AND 5 cm from Q simultaneously!
So pair your ruler (straight edges) with a compass (exact distances) to construct curves, squares, rectangles and houses cleanly!

problem.en: You need point X to be exactly 4 cm from point A and 4 cm from point B (where AB = 6 cm). How does a compass find X?

text.en: Draw segment AB = 6 cm with a ruler.

why.en: This sets the base distance between A and B.

text.en: Open the compass to 4 cm, put the tip at A, and draw an arc above AB.

why.en: Every point on this arc is 4 cm from A.

text.en: Keep the compass at 4 cm, put the tip at B, and cross the first arc at X.

why.en: Intersection X sits at exact distance 4 cm from both A and B.

prompt.en: Why would opening the compass to only 2 cm from A and 2 cm from B fail to cross when AB = 6 cm?

requiredIdeas.en: 2 cm + 2 cm = 4 cm, which is shorter than 6 cm.
The two arcs will stay separated with a 2 cm gap in the middle!

commonMisconceptions.en: Two arcs always meet regardless of length.

points.en: Circle/arc keeps every point at equal distance (radius) from centre.
Compass transfers exact distances without reading approximations.
Rectangles have 90° corners and equal bisecting diagonals.
Equidistant points sit where equal-radius compass arcs intersect.
